appraisal_events.evidence: Cet excellent homme souffrait d'être trouvé si ennuyeux par les Verdurin... Il capitula si vite, eut l'air si malheureux de voir manqué l'effet sur lequel il avait compté et répondit d'un ton si lâche à Swann : « C'est bon, c'est bon ; en tous cas, même si je me trompe, ce n'est pas un crime, je pense ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Saniette invents an anecdote to amuse the table, but when Swann's sympathetic correction threatens to expose the fabrication, Saniette collapses abjectly and capitulates in a craven tone, revealing his desperate, habitually failed need to entertain the Verdurins.

appraisal_events.evidence: À peine avait-il commencé à faire le mouvement de tête et d'épaules de quelqu'un qui s'esclaffe qu'aussitôt il se mettait à tousser... Ainsi lui et Mme Verdurin... avaient l'air de deux masques de théâtre qui figuraient différemment la gaîté.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator ironically reduces M. Verdurin's hilarity to a rehearsed physical routine (coughing on pipe smoke), comparing him and Mme Verdurin to theatrical masks merely performing gaiety rather than feeling it.

appraisal_events.evidence: Mais Mme de Crécy, voilà une petite femme qui a l'air intelligente, ah ! saperlipopette, on voit tout de suite qu'elle a l'œil américain, celle-là !
appraisal_events.explanation: Forcheville praises Odette's sharpness and allure enthusiastically to Cottard, favoring her by contrast with his more lukewarm remark that Mme Verdurin is already showing her age.

status_effects.explanation: Saniette is shown visibly desperate to succeed at entertaining the group and collapses into craven backpedaling the moment his fabrication is threatened, a clear local emotional diminishment.
The narrator's ironic description of his coughing-laughter as a rehearsed 'mask' of gaiety mildly deflates him as performing sociability rather than feeling it.
Forcheville's enthusiastic, if crude, praise of her intelligence and allure marks her favorably in this male conversation, though absent from it herself.

ambiguities: The 'masques de théâtre' comparison could be read as affectionate comic characterization of the Verdurins' habitual manner rather than a genuine narratorial diminishment of their sincerity.

Forcheville's admiration of Odette shades into crude physical objectification (interrupted by Cottard's stock joke before he finishes describing her body), so the praise is not unambiguously flattering.
